name: Zhen Zhang
affiliation: Division of Applied Mathematics, Brown University
tagline: I work on scientific machine learning for fluid mechanics — learning turbulence closures from sparse data, and asking when neural methods genuinely beat the classical ones.
bio: I am a postdoctoral research associate in the Division of Applied Mathematics at Brown University, working with George Em Karniadakis. I received my bachelor's and Ph.D. degrees from the Department of Energy and Power Engineering at Tsinghua University.

My research sits between computational fluid dynamics and machine learning. I build physics-informed methods that infer turbulence closures and flow fields from sparse, noisy experimental data, and I care about the part that is easy to skip: testing whether a learned model generalizes beyond the configuration it was trained on, and comparing new methods against classical adjoint-based optimization under conditions fair enough for the comparison to mean something.

Before moving to applied mathematics, I spent several years on gas-turbine film cooling — vortex dynamics, in-hole flow physics, and data-driven models for turbulent heat transport. That work still shapes how I think about closure modeling.

news.text: Preprint: Generalizable turbulence closures across bluff-body shapes by PINN-based solver-agnostic training.
Turbulence closure in RANS and flow inference around a cylinder using PINNs and sparse experimental data appears in the Journal of Fluid Mechanics.
Effect of turbulence-closure consistency on airfoil identification appears in Computers & Fluids.
Presented two talks at the 78th Annual Meeting of the APS Division of Fluid Dynamics.
PINNs with coordinate transformation for high Reynolds number boundary layer flows appears in the Journal of Computational Physics.

software.name: adjoint_PINN_inverse_comparison
software.description: Source code, benchmark configurations and data for the controlled comparison of adjoint optimization and PINNs on PDE-constrained inverse problems: unsteady Burgers, noisy Darcy permeability inversion, 3D Allen–Cahn reaction identification, and unsteady Navier–Stokes viscosity identification.

software.name: mySU2
software.description: Personal development branch of SU2, the open-source multiphysics simulation and design suite, used for adjoint-based sensitivity analysis and solver-coupled closure training.
